matchup: Connecticut Sun at Los Angeles Sparks

halftime_diagnostics.key_read: The 80-point halftime total was inflated by Los Angeles' 32-point first quarter on 78.6% shooting. Q2 collapsed to 26 combined points. SharpEdge projected 76 second-half points before seeing the sportsbook, while William Hill's 162.5 implied approximately 82.5 second-half points. Both team-total projections also sat below market, supporting the full-game Under rather than relying on a single-team regression thesis.

what_we_got_right: The market-blind 156 total was directionally and structurally correct before sportsbook comparison; the game finished 145.
The full-game market offered 162.5, creating a 6.5-point pre-wager edge versus SharpEdge fair and a 17.5-point final cushion.
Both team totals were projected below the sportsbook numbers, which made the full-game Under a cleaner derivative than isolating only one team.
The first-quarter 54-point scoring burst was correctly treated as unstable rather than the new game regime. The next three quarters produced only 26, 32 and 33 combined points.
Los Angeles' Q1 78.6% field-goal shooting regressed sharply and did not re-establish itself as a sustainable scoring environment.
Connecticut's weak perimeter offense persisted: 15.4% from three at halftime and 16.7% for the full game.
The projected 76-point second half was conservative relative to the market's implied 82.5 and the actual second half came in even lower at 65.
important_game_mechanics: Connecticut scored only 10 points in Q3 on 25.0% shooting, preserving the Under even while Los Angeles scored efficiently in the quarter.
Los Angeles then scored only 11 points in Q4 and committed 10 fourth-quarter turnovers.
Los Angeles finished with 25 turnovers and Connecticut recorded 15 steals, but those extra-possession events did not convert into enough efficient offense to threaten the total.

Dearica Hamby was ejected on a flagrant-2 with 8:39 remaining in Q4. This was a post-wager event that likely added downside to Los Angeles scoring, but it was not part of the original edge and should not receive credit in the pre-wager model assessment.
risk_notes: The final result should not cause the model to over-tighten totals simply because this Under won by a large margin. The pre-wager edge was 6.5 points, not 17.5 points.

Los Angeles' 25 turnovers and Connecticut's 15 steals represent a transition-volatility pathway that can sometimes create Overs. The fact that it did not here reflects poor conversion, not the absence of risk.
Late-game ejection and game-state effects widened the final Under margin and should be treated as realized variance rather than repeatable forecast signal.

model_reinforcement.name: LIVEFLOW_HALFTIME_REGIME_CONFIRMATION_v1
rules: When a high-scoring first quarter is followed by a materially slower second quarter, do not anchor the live total to the first-half average. Separate quarter regimes and identify which one is supported by sustainable possession and efficiency signals.
Prefer the full-game total when both independently projected team totals point in the same direction versus market; this reduces team-share allocation risk.
Continue requiring market-blind projection before sportsbook comparison and preserve the frozen fair number in the audit trail.

Track persistent three-point inefficiency separately from raw field-goal percentage. A team that is generating attempts but failing badly from three can suppress the total even if two-point scoring remains functional.
Do not retroactively attribute edge to ejections, injuries or other post-wager events. Log them as realized variance unless they were visible at execution.

postmortem.lesson: This was the cleaner version of the LIVE-FLOW total process: build the fair number first, identify that both team scoring shares sit below market, then attack the combined total. The 162.5 market required 82.5 second-half points while SharpEdge projected 76; only 65 were scored. The win validates the structure more than the final 17.5-point margin.

execution_notes: SharpEdge projected its own lines before sportsbook comparison.
William Hill live total at execution: 162.5, Under -115.
Primary market gap: 6.5 points toward the Under.
Los Angeles team-total projection: 83 versus market 85.5.
Spread was considered efficient: SharpEdge Los Angeles -10 versus market -9.5, so no spread wager was recommended.
Official final: Los Angeles 77, Connecticut 68; total 145.
